title: Even-order Grünschloß–Keller permutation nets: net property and tiling distance
summary: This Lean development proves that the even-order permutation construction of Grünschloß and Keller (MCQMC 2008 proceedings, implemented in gendiag0m2.h) is a base-2 (0,m,2)-net for every even m >= 4. The proof is symbolic: for every resolution a it proves, for every even m >= 8, that one explicit pair of points has squared distance 241 * 2^(m-8), and at m = 8 that 241 is the exact minimum over all pairs and all lattice translates. The exhaustive m = 8 lower bound is reduced by ordinary kernel decide; the exactness of the computed candidate minimum over the whole lattice is a symbolic lemma.…

formalizes.title: The Even-Order Grünschloß–Keller Permutation Nets Are (0,m,2)-Nets

review.reason: Lean proof that a permutation construction gives a base-2 digital net with stated distance bounds.
